Bug_Title: Eq: equals() method defined that doesn’t override equals(Object) (EQ_OTHER_NO_OBJECT)
Bug_Details:
This class defines an equals()
method, that doesn't override the normal equals(Object) method
defined in the base java.lang.Object class.  Instead, it
inherits an equals(Object) method from a superclass.
The class should probably define a boolean equals(Object) method.
 equals() equals(Object) java.lang.Object equals(Object) boolean equals(Object)
Bug_Explanation: The equals() method in MyClass doesn't override the equals(Object) method defined in the base java.lang.Object class. Instead, it inherits an equals(Object) method from a superclass. The class should probably define a boolean equals(Object) method.
Trigger_Explanation: This test case triggers the bug because the equals() method in MyClass doesn't override the equals(Object) method from java.lang.Object. This causes the equals() method to use Object's equals method instead, which performs reference equality. The test case then calls showBug() and expects true, but due to the bug, it returns false.
